subject: owl
pitch: A great horned owl perched on a gnarled branch. Mottled bark-brown and buff feathers with fine dark barring, a pale bib at the throat, tall feathered ear tufts, a round tawny facial disc rimmed in black, huge orange eyes and a hooked grey beak. Feathered legs end in strong black talons gripping the wood.
reasoning:
I need to plan the owl module efficiently, working out the perch geometry so the owl's feet sit properly atop the gnarled branch, which itself needs to touch the floor at y=0.

Now I'm sketching the joint hierarchy: a pelvis root, a spine chain curving up to the chest, a short neck leading to head and jaw joints, a downward-curving tail for the perched pose, and leg chains with hips bent to grip the branch.

Still designing the leg and toe rigging...

Now I'm thinking through the wings — folded against the body but kept slightly separated per the extended-pose requirement, built as a chain from shoulder down and back, to be lofted into a wing shape.

Defining wing outline points...

Attaching the wing bone at the shoulder joint and keeping it rigid. Now I'm working out the body loft stations from pelvis up through the bulbous breast, defining width and height at each station to get that upright teardrop owl silhouette, and figuring out the orientation axes for the sweep path.

Adding more body stations...

Still writing body paint logic...

Now I'm shaping the head: a flattened sphere scaled for width and height, positioned above the body, with facial discs made from flattened cylinders colored tawny with black rims.

Still working out positioning...

For the pupil, I'll position it slightly in front of the eye surface along the normal direction so it sits visibly on top, then consider adding a thin black ring for extra definition around the eye.

Now I'm planning the ear tufts as tall feathered spikes swept upward from the head, using a path of points with tapering radius to create a leaf-like shape when viewed from the front.

Still writing beak geometry...

Now I'm adding a separate cream-colored throat bib positioned at the chest, sized small and placed just below the head front, with fine stripes for texture. I'm also considering a dark chest-band but deciding to skip it since belly barring already covers that, then moving to blend the head gradient into the neck/body top.

For the legs, I'm setting up feathered thighs as a tapered sweep chain (hip, knee, ankle joints) with buff barred coloring, positioning them symmetrically around x=±0.06 to fit the body width, and defining a radius array that tapers from thigh to ankle.

Now I'm working out foot placement on the branch, with toes extending forward and backward from the foot center, wrapping down over the branch's curved surface toward the ground.

Still working out toe geometry...

Adding the spike tip for the toe and attaching the branch geometry to the pelvis joint, wobbling the path along x with varying y/z offsets.

I'm adjusting the branch's radius and center height so it doesn't dip below ground, aiming for a centerline around y .05 with the foot resting near y .098.

I'm planning small side twigs sweeping off the main branch with tapering radii, plus bark paint using mottled brown grain textures and a greenish lichen patch for moss, and setting up the bone hierarchy starting from a pelvis root for each branch.

Now I'm working out the tail: a chain of three points hanging behind the body, built as a flat fan-shaped sweep with wide-then-thin radius profiles to give it a feathered look from behind.

I'm adding striping along the tail's length with round caps at the start and flat caps at the tip for a feather edge, deciding to skip finer details like separation lines or gradient bands for now and moving on to set up the wings with a shoulder-elbow-wrist joint chain per side.

Still placing wing geometry...

Defining the wing outline points...

I'll mark the tip as sharp and keep smoothing at 0 with enough points to avoid crossing issues near the narrow point, using a bevel of .012 and tapering the thickness from thin at the tip to thicker toward the base. For mirroring left/right, I'm working out the normal direction via cross product to get the correct orientation.

For the wing coloring, I'm layering barred brown stripes across the flight feathers with mottled texture, then adding a second covert layer offset outward with spotted buff-cream detailing. Still writing covert layer outline...

Separately, I'm attaching the wing mesh to the shoulder bone and now adding the facial disc rim — a black outer disc beneath a tawny inner disc, sized and embedded to sit flush on the head.

Adjusting the embed depths and heights so the black disc sinks lower while the tawny disc sits slightly higher, matching the tilted surface normals along the head. I'm also setting the head's overall proportions and positioning the eye hit points symmetrically on either side.

I'm sizing the low-poly head sphere and scaling it to shape, then working through color/paint mapping for chest barring stripes and the body loft, including the bone chain and pelvis ring stations along the spine.

I'm also repositioning the pelvis root slightly to avoid overlapping with the spine path, then defining the spine chain points (spine1 through spine3) and starting the neck chain extending from the spine tip.

Setting up the neck joints with parent spine3, then adding head and jaw joints with appropriate aim directions and positions, letting the spine chain default to pelvis as its nearest parent.

I'm checking the overall proportions against a great horned owl's build—realizing the ear tufts make the owl too tall, so I'm shrinking the tuft height from base .64 to tip .72 to keep the total height more realistic relative to the branch.

For the tail, I'm connecting its chain to the pelvis joint as the parent since that's the nearest anatomical point. Then I'm working out the toe layout for each foot, using mirrored side loops to place two forward toes and a zygodactyl back toe pair with small offset distances from the foot's center.

I'm checking that the toe positions actually sit on the branch surface rather than floating or clipping through it, so each toe's y and z coordinates are computed against the branch's curved radius at that height to get a natural gripping pose.

Still defining toe geometry...

Now I'm setting up the leg sweep using the ankle joint chain, with feather-leg points tapering from thigh to ankle and radii shrinking down to the foot, keeping it mostly hidden within the body silhouette.

Still defining the wing chain...

Still defining the tuft sweep...

Still placing head geometry and eye sockets...

Adding a highlight sphere positioned relative to the eye normal, then sketching small cream bristle spikes near the lores, and starting to build the hooked upper beak as a swept curve through a few control points.

Refining the beak geometry: upper mandible gets a gradient from light to dark grey with a pointed hooked tip, while the lower mandible is a shorter, thinner swept shape positioned just beneath it so the jaws align naturally.

For the tail I'll extend into branches and twigs, using simple catmull chains for the tuft sweep, and keep the outline points as plain typed tuples without smoothing since the extrude builder doesn't need curve types here -- just straightforward arrays.
